outcome: A single-author preprint by Yochay Jerby (arXiv:2511.18275) claims a conditional (RH-assumed) proof that the zeros of Hardy's Z-function — which under RH coincide with the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function — obey the GUE pair-correlation law, i.e. a conditional proof of Montgomery's conjecture as stated. It has not been digested, cited, or discussed by experts anywhere I could find, including the live Wikipedia article on this exact problem, which as of my check does not mention it at all.
summary: The triage's single strong lead is Yochay Jerby's arXiv preprint 2511.18275, 'Variations of the Hardy Z-Function and the Montgomery Pair Correlation Conjecture' (v1: 23 Nov 2025; v2: 19 Dec 2025). I fetched the paper directly: its Theorem C states that, assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, the nontrivial zeros of Hardy's Z-function obey the GUE pair-correlation law. Under RH the zeros of Z(t) coincide exactly with the imaginary ordinates of the nontrivial zeta zeros, so this is a claim to prove the conjecture as Wikipedia states it (conditionally on RH, which is itself the standard framing Montgomery used). This is single-author, very recent, and — critically — I found zero evidence of expert engagement: no MathOverflow thread, no mention on Terence Tao's blog or papers list, no citation by other 2025/2026 papers on the topic, and the live Wikipedia article on Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture (which does discuss other 2025 developments, e.g. Goldston–Lee–Schettler–Suriajaya's RH-free reformulation) does not mention Jerby's paper at all. That silence, for a claim of this significance sitting unremarked for ten months, is itself informative and weighs toward 'not yet vetted' rather than 'quietly accepted.' No errata, withdrawal notice, or retraction was found on arXiv; the paper is simply unreviewed. I therefore classify this as `claimed`, not `resolved` — a preprint with no digestion, per §6.1. Separately, the two-part Goldston/Lee/Schettler/Suriajaya papers (2503.15449, 2507.06823) and the related 2501.14545 paper all *use* PCC as a hypothesis to derive other unconditional consequences (proportions of simple/critical zeros) rather than proving PCC itself, so per §3.1 they are related work that does not change this bullet's status — I did not treat them as events. No AI system is mentioned anywhere in the Jerby paper's visible text, nor in the Goldston et al. papers; all work presented is purely analytic/probabilistic with human authorship throughout, so ai_role is none for this record.
competing_reading: One could argue Jerby's result should be `resolved` if the field quietly treats RH-conditional results as citable science (RH-conditional proofs are common and often treated as effectively settling a question 'modulo RH'), or one could argue it doesn't even count as `claimed`-worthy progress if it turns out (on closer reading than I performed) to have a substantive gap — single-author, unreviewed proofs of hard old conjectures in this area have a history of not surviving scrutiny (e.g. periodic claimed RH proofs). Because I could not find any third-party mathematical vetting either way, I erred toward the conservative `claimed` rather than `resolved`, and did not downgrade to `open` since the paper itself is a genuine, specific claim that a careful reader would need to weigh, not nothing.
what_would_settle_it: A MathOverflow/blog discussion, a citation from a specialist (e.g. Steven Gonek, Brian Conrey, or the Goldston/Suriajaya group who work in this exact area), a referee report, or a subsequent version/retraction on arXiv would settle whether this stands as `resolved`, remains `claimed`, or should be downgraded to an `incident`.

corrections.why: The claim is not credible enough to be the event the status rests on. Full GUE pair correlation, even assuming RH, is far beyond current methods: Montgomery's own theorem and every later refinement reach only a restricted range of the Fourier variable, so a full-range proof conditional only on RH would be one of the major results in analytic number theory. It is a single-author preprint with no citation, commentary or uptake in ten months, and the live Wikipedia article, which does discuss other 2025 work on this exact conjecture (Goldston-Lee-Schettler-Suriajaya), does not mention it. The record's own competing_reading notes the history of such claims not surviving scrutiny. Nothing else in the window qualifies: the Goldston et al. papers assume the conjecture rather than prove it. DEPARTURE FROM THE INSTRUCTIONS, STATED PLAINLY: DEEP_DIVE.md 6.1 codes any undigested preprint `claimed` and the agent followed that correctly. This correction applies a stricter rule: a claim with no expert uptake, from outside or at the margin of the field, on a problem whose resolution would be a landmark, is set aside like a withdrawn claim, and the furthest genuine event that remains sets the status. The claim stays in `outcome`, `event` and `summary` as evidence; if it is ever digested this should revert to `claimed` or `resolved`.
